meta.titre: Milk and Milk Products: Composition, Uses in the Diet, Heat Treatment and Cooking
meta.sous_theme: Composition and uses of milk, milk products, handling and cooking

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A mother in a town buys a tin of powdered milk for the baby, fresh milk from a farmer for the family, and yoghurt as a snack for the children. Milk is one of the few foods that a baby can live on for months, so the examiners treat it as a model food. They ask what milk contains, why it is called a nearly perfect food, how its products are made, and how to store and cook it. Paper 2 often asks you to outline and explain a fixed number of its uses in the diet.

items: Proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals and water are the nutrients in food.
Calcium is needed for strong bones and teeth.
Bacteria multiply quickly in warm, moist, protein foods.

sections.titre: Milk: what it contains, what it is used for and its products
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Composition of cow's milk
| Nutrient | In milk |
|---|---|
| Water | Makes up most of the milk |
| Protein | Casein and lactalbumin: first class protein for growth and repair |
| Fat | Butterfat in tiny droplets that rise as cream; gives energy and carries vitamins A and D |
| Carbohydrate | Lactose, the milk sugar, for energy |
| Vitamins | A and D in the fat, and B group vitamins; very little vitamin C |
| Minerals | Calcium and phosphorus for bones and teeth; very little iron |

Milk is called a nearly perfect food because it contains most of the nutrients the body needs in good proportions. It is not completely perfect because it is poor in iron and vitamin C and has no fibre.

### Uses of milk in the diet
1. Body building: its protein supports growth and repairs worn tissue, so it suits children and pregnant women.
2. Strong bones and teeth: calcium and phosphorus.
3. Energy: lactose and butterfat.
4. Protection: vitamin A helps the eyes and skin, and vitamin D helps the body to use calcium.
5. Cooking: it is used in sauces, puddings, custard, cakes, soups and drinks, and adds flavour and food value.
6. Breast milk is the best food for a young baby. The first thick yellowish milk, colostrum, contains antibodies that protect the newborn from infection.

### Milk products
Cream (fat from the top of milk); butter (cream churned); cheese (milk curdled, then the solid curds are separated from the liquid whey); yoghurt (milk soured by harmless bacteria that turn lactose into lactic acid); evaporated milk (part of the water removed, canned); condensed milk (water removed and sugar added); dried milk (all the water removed, which keeps for a long time while dry).

variantes.nom: Heat treatment, buying and storing milk
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how milk is made safe or how to store it.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Raw milk can carry harmful bacteria. Pasteurisation heats milk to a moderate temperature for a set time and cools it quickly, which kills most harmful bacteria with little change of taste. Sterilised milk is heated at a higher temperature in sealed bottles and keeps longer. UHT milk is heated to a very high temperature for a few seconds and keeps for months until opened. At home keep milk covered and cold, away from strong smells, use the oldest first, and treat made-up dried milk like fresh milk. Buy from a clean seller and check the date.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for rules or faults when milk is heated.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Milk protein sets with heat, so a skin forms on top and a layer can stick and burn at the base. Heat slowly, stir, use a saucepan rinsed with cold water, and watch it because it boils over quickly. Acid foods such as lemon juice or very sour fruit can make milk curdle. Cooking also reduces some vitamins.

sections.enonce_markdown: Outline and explain three ways in which milk helps the health of a growing child. (6 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Outline" gives the point, "explain" gives the reason, and 6 marks for three points means 2 marks for each, one for the point and one for the explanation.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Three points, each with a reason.

etapes.action: List the useful nutrients in milk.
etapes.justification: A good answer links a nutrient to its job in a child's body.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Protein, calcium and phosphorus, vitamins A and D, lactose and fat.

etapes.justification: Different uses avoid repeating the same idea and show wide knowledge.

etapes.action: Write each use with a reason.
etapes.justification: The reason should name the nutrient and say what it does.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Growth: the first class protein builds new body cells. 2. Bones and teeth: calcium and phosphorus make them hard and strong, helped by vitamin D. 3. Energy: lactose and fat are burned to give energy for play and study.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Milk supports growth through its first class protein; it builds strong bones and teeth because it supplies calcium and phosphorus, with vitamin D to help their use; and it gives energy from lactose and butterfat.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that milk is a perfect food because it contains iron and vitamin C in large amounts.
items.pourquoi_faux: Milk has very little iron and vitamin C.
items.correction_markdown: Say that milk is a nearly perfect food because it contains most nutrients in good proportions, but it is poor in iron and vitamin C.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing four uses of milk without any explanation when the question says "outline and explain".
items.pourquoi_faux: Half the marks are for the explanation.
items.correction_markdown: Write each use followed by the nutrient and its function, for example: "Bone building, because calcium and phosphorus make the bones hard."

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that pasteurised milk is completely free from all bacteria.
items.pourquoi_faux: Pasteurisation kills most harmful bacteria, not all of them; sterilising kills nearly all.
items.correction_markdown: Say that pasteurisation kills most harmful bacteria, and that pasteurised milk still needs to be kept cold.

items.erreur_markdown: Mixing up the products, for example saying yoghurt is made by churning.
items.pourquoi_faux: Churned cream is butter; yoghurt is made by bacteria acting on milk.
items.correction_markdown: Butter: churning cream. Cheese: curdling milk. Yoghurt: fermenting milk with bacteria.

items.erreur_markdown: Heating milk quickly on high heat and leaving it alone.
items.pourquoi_faux: It forms a skin, sticks to the pan and boils over.
items.correction_markdown: Heat it slowly, stir it, and watch it.

items.enonce_markdown: Name (a) the sugar found in milk, (b) the main mineral in milk that builds bones and teeth, (c) the product made when cream is churned, and (d) the process that makes yoghurt from milk.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Lactose**. (b) **Calcium**. (c) **Butter**. (d) **Fermentation by harmless bacteria (which change lactose to lactic acid)**.

items.enonce_markdown: A tin of dried milk of mass 400 g costs $2\,800$ FCFA. One glass of milk is made from 25 g of the powder. Fresh milk costs $900$ FCFA per litre and a glass holds 200 ml (assumed prices). (a) How many glasses does one tin make? (b) Find the cost of one glass from powder. (c) Find the cost of one glass of fresh milk. (d) A family drinks 2 glasses a day for 30 days. How much does it save in 30 days by using the cheaper kind?
items.solution_markdown: (a) $400 \div 25 = 16$, so **16 glasses**. (b) $2\,800 \div 16 = 175$, so **$175$ FCFA**. (c) $1\,000 \div 200 = 5$ glasses in a litre, and $900 \div 5 = 180$, so **$180$ FCFA**. (d) The powder is cheaper by $180 - 175 = 5$ FCFA per glass. Glasses drunk: $2 \times 30 = 60$. Saving: $5 \times 60 = 300$, so **$300$ FCFA**.

items.enonce_markdown: A family buys a pot of yoghurt at $250$ FCFA for each of the 3 children every day. A neighbour suggests making yoghurt at home from 1 litre of milk costing $700$ FCFA, which fills 5 pots (assumed prices). (a) Find the cost of buying 3 pots a day for 7 days. (b) Find the cost of one home-made pot and of the same quantity for 7 days. (c) How much is saved in the week? (d) Explain why home-made yoghurt still needs clean equipment and cold storage.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $250 \times 3 \times 7 = 5\,250$, so **$5\,250$ FCFA**. (b) One pot: $700 \div 5 = 140$, so $140$ FCFA. Seven days: $140 \times 3 \times 7 = 2\,940$, so **$2\,940$ FCFA**. (c) $5\,250 - 2\,940 = 2\,310$, so **$2\,310$ FCFA** is saved. (d) Milk is rich in protein and moisture, so harmful bacteria also grow quickly in it if the utensils are dirty or the yoghurt is left warm. Clean utensils prevent contamination and storing it cold slows the growth of bacteria.

items_markdown: Milk contains protein, fat, lactose, vitamins A, D and B group, calcium and phosphorus; it is poor in iron and vitamin C.
It is called a nearly perfect food because it contains most nutrients in good proportions.
Uses in the diet: growth and repair, bones and teeth, energy, protection, cooking; colostrum protects a newborn baby with antibodies.
Products: cream, butter (churned cream), cheese (curds), yoghurt (fermented), evaporated, condensed and dried milk.
Pasteurisation kills most harmful bacteria; sterilised and UHT milk keep longer; keep milk covered and cold.
Cook milk slowly and stir; for "outline and explain" give each use with its reason.
